name: Getting Your Bathroom Waterproofing Right the First Time
description: Getting Your Bathroom Waterproofing Right the First Time

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Getting your bathroom waterproofing done correctly the first time can save you a ton of trouble and expense down the line. It's a critical step that often gets underestimated! The process kicks off with a solid assessment and planning phase. We pinpoint all the 'wet zones' – that’s your shower floor, walls up to the showerhead, and around the bath – checking your substrate and any transitions like corners and curb. Choosing the right waterproofing system, whether it’s a sheet or liquid membrane, that plays nice with your chosen tile and substrate is key. Next, it’s all about surface preparation: getting everything super clean, dry, and making any necessary repairs. Then comes the membrane installation itself. For sheet membranes, it’s precise measuring and overlapping seams, while liquid membranes require uniform coats with proper drying time in between. We pay extra attention to detailing wet areas like shower floors and walls, ensuring proper slope to the drain, and securely integrating the pan liner or membrane into the drain. The final, super important step is curing and testing. The membrane needs to cure fully, usually 24-48 hours, before tiling. And for shower pans, we always do a flood test, filling it with water for about 24 hours to make absolutely sure there are no leaks. It sounds like a lot, but this thorough approach is how you guarantee a long-lasting, leak-free bathroom. If you're planning a bathroom remodel, make sure your contractor emphasizes this process and can walk you through each step to ensure peace of mind.
